correctness.rationale: The normal covector under the affine map is A^(1/2)u, of length sqrt(q). The hyperplane volume multiplier is sqrt(det A)/sqrt(q); the ball slice at signed distance (±1−t)/sqrt(q) gives the remaining power and hence the q^(−d/2) factor. Interior containment gives q>(1+|t|)^2. On the allowed interval h(x)=log(q−x²) is strictly concave, so [h(1−t)+h(1+t)]/2≤h(1), strictly unless t=0. The centered profile has log derivative (d−q)/(2q(q−1)), hence the unique optimum at q=d, with the stated constant. All-direction equality forces c=0,A=dI; equality of the spherical geometric mean forces all-direction equality by continuity and full support. For any other λ>1, a centered determinant-preserving perturbation along the first diagonal entry of diag(1,−1,0,…) with signed ε moving q towards d improves the section pair; λ>1 keeps strict containment for small ε. At (d,0) the first derivatives vanish and the log-pair Hessian is diagonal with entries −1/[2d(d−1)] and −(d+1)/(d−1). Substitution of q−d=εd uᵀHu+O(ε²) and t=εu·b and the fourth and second spherical moments reproduce both quadratic coefficients, uniformly by compactness of the sphere. The integrated deficit has strictly positive coefficients on tr(H²) and ||b||², including d=2.
residual_risks: This is a local integrated Hessian, not a global stability estimate or an inequality for arbitrary convex bodies; the analytic verification does not depend on the sampled matrices.

value.rationale: The geometric comparison has a natural constraint and statistic: fixed enclosing volume, paired sections by the inner ball's two opposite supports. It identifies an exceptional radius, gives the exact directional equality condition even for translated bodies, and separates the shape and translation costs in the logarithmic averaged deficit. This is useful sharp local information about a natural extremum, not novelty in the affine section formula or a claim of global metric stability.
residual_risks: Elementary and limited to ellipsoids; neither a general convex-body extremum nor a new reconstruction theorem.
